subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should the experimental `claws remove` contract deliberately delete completed active provenance without a retained redacted tombstone, relying on partial subordinate rows only for failed cleanup recovery?
rationale: The discussion contains a direct contract disagreement about operator recovery and post-removal explainability; source review cannot safely choose between a minimal active-state model and a retained audit/recovery artifact without RFC or maintainer intent.

options.title: Confirm no-tombstone lifecycle
options.body: Keep completed removal stateless, document the loss of post-removal explainability, and require the final cleanup proof before merging.

options.title: Define a bounded recovery record
options.body: Add an explicit redacted, SQLite-backed removal record with a documented retention and privacy contract before accepting lifecycle deletion.

options.title: Defer removal scope
options.body: Keep status and planning separate and postpone destructive removal until the recovery model is settled.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded recovery record
recommendation.body: Add an explicit redacted, SQLite-backed removal record with a documented retention and privacy contract before accepting lifecycle deletion.

likelyOwner.reason: The removal-ownership requirement was raised through the RFC review context and is the closest supplied signal for the lifecycle contract decision.
